The Wall Street Journal on Thursday cast doubt on Donald Trump’s meeting with Russia’s Vladimir Putin and China’s Xi Jinping, suggesting the trio’s joint declaration on nuclear peace was little more than rhetoric.

The newspaper’s conservative editorial board acknowledged — in a piece titled “Nuclear Peace In Our Time. Not.” — that the summit in China “could have been worse,” noting that Trump appeared “to have conceded nothing on Ukraine or Taiwan.”

But it warned that Putin remains “the biggest nuclear risk on the planet today,” citing his repeated threats to deploy tactical nukes in Ukraine, which Russia invaded in 2022.

The Journal, a frequent needler of Trump in his second term, questioned whether his personal rapport with Xi could curb China’s expanding nuclear arsenal. And it criticized the president for downplaying Russian and Chinese support for Iran, against which the U.S. launched a war in February.

The board also urged Trump to boost America’s nuclear deterrent and argued “the best nuclear nonproliferation project on the table today is to win the war with Iran in a convincing way” that Russia and China cannot ignore.
